evidence.requirements: Every brief item is met. The start page shows title, date and time, price and "<n> seats left" (Home.tsx:19-31, start.jpg). Each card has a "Book <title>" link (Home.tsx:33-35). The form has fields labelled Name, Email and Guests, a Book button, and guests limited to 1-8 (Book.tsx:131-158, booking-schema.ts:10-14). The server enforces the seat limit and shows the error under the Guests field (store.ts:37-38, app.ts:72). The confirmation shows the heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (Book.tsx:31-45, confirmation.jpg: Red Wine Cellar Tour, 2 guests, EUR 64). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, and the password comes from STAFF_PASSWORD (Staff.tsx:32-45, index.ts:4). Bookings are grouped by tasting with name, email, guests, reference and Cancel (Staff.tsx:50-96, staff.jpg), and cancelling frees seats (store.ts:44). Error, success and fully booked states exist (styles.css notice-*, badge), there is a phone layout (styles.css:423-452), and the app uses React, Express, react-router, react-hook-form and zod.
evidence.correctness: book() is synchronous, so the seat check and insert cannot interleave, and a concurrency test proves it (store.ts:33-41, app.test.ts:82-91). Zod rejects 0, 1.5, the string "2", null and -1, and validation is the same on client and server (shared/booking-schema.ts). Cancelling deletes the booking, so the seat count recomputes; cancelling twice returns 404 (app.test.ts:149). After a 409 the form reloads the seat count (Book.tsx:101). Minor flaws: seatsMessage yields "Only 1 seats left for this tasting" (booking-schema.ts:31), and a fully booked tasting still shows an active form that can only fail (Book.tsx:120-159).
evidence.security: The password is compared with timingSafeEqual on SHA-256 digests, and an empty STAFF_PASSWORD disables sign-in (app.ts:27,94). The session is regenerated on sign-in to prevent fixation (app.ts:97). The cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and Secure:auto. The session has a fixed 8 h lifetime that use does not extend (app.ts:44,48-52). Sign-in is rate-limited to 5 failures per 15 min (app.ts:83-90). The app uses helmet, a 10kb JSON limit, Cache-Control no-store on the API, and a generic 500 handler. The session secret is random and nothing secret is in the code. React escapes all output. Staff routes are guarded by requireStaff (app.ts:110-114). Minor: it uses the default express-session MemoryStore.
evidence.code_quality: The structure is clean and small: server/app.ts, store.ts and tastings.ts, a shared zod schema used on both sides, a thin api.ts client, and three pages. Naming is clear, comments are sparse and purposeful (store.ts:10,13,33). Errors are handled: field errors map to setError, there are 401/404 paths in Staff, and load-failure states with retry (Home.tsx:58-64). There is no needless abstraction.
evidence.tests: server/app.test.ts has about 20 Supertest cases. They cover the listing, totals and references, per-field validation, guests boundary values, overbooking, a full tasting, concurrent booking, 404 and malformed JSON, staff 401, wrong and empty passwords, grouping, cancel freeing seats, logout, expiry, rate limiting and cookie flags. e2e/bookings.spec.ts runs the full guest and staff flows in a browser and checks accessible descriptions of errors, plus a no-horizontal-scroll check at 375 px. test-results/.last-run.json shows passed.
evidence.ux_design: The look is clearly winery-themed: a burgundy header with a gold rule, cream background, and date stubs on cards (start.jpg). The inline field error is clear, with a red border and "Error: Enter a valid email address" (form.jpg). The green success panel with a summary list is clear (confirmation.jpg). Weaknesses: dates are raw ISO "2026-11-06 18:00", there are no imagery or descriptions of the tastings, and the confirmation page is sparse.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are tied via htmlFor/id, and errors are linked with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, with role=alert (Book.tsx:10-21,132-153). The form focuses the first invalid field, the confirmation focuses its heading (Book.tsx:26-28), and a status region gets focus after a cancel (Staff.tsx:119). There is a skip link, lang=en, a caption-free table with scope=col, an sr-only Actions header, and Cancel buttons described by the booking name. The decorative stub and meter are aria-hidden. Text contrast looks good. Weaknesses: the gold focus outline #b08d57 on cream is about 2.6:1, under the 3:1 needed for focus indicators, and on phones the hidden thead removes column header semantics.
evidence.simplicity: Dependencies are few and conventional: express, express-session, express-rate-limit, helmet, react, react-router, react-hook-form, zod. The code is roughly 800 lines in total for the whole app plus tests, which fits the problem. The esbuild server bundle is a single build script line.
evidence.maintainability: README covers run, environment variables, tests and the openspec specs, and a lockfile exists. Missing: no CI pipeline, no changelog or release/versioning approach beyond version 1.0.0, no ADRs (only specs), and no staff manual. The Node version is loose (engines ">=22", no .nvmrc), and dependencies use caret ranges. Build artifacts and .playwright-mcp screenshots were delivered in the folder (they are gitignored).
evidence.visual_design: Typography is consistent: Georgia serif headings, system sans body, monospace references. The burgundy, gold and cream palette is used consistently on all pages, and buttons and cards are consistent (start.jpg, staff.jpg). It looks finished but plain: no imagery or logo, and the ISO dates look technical.
evidence.layout: Hierarchy is clear: H1, intro, then a three-card grid (start.jpg). The form is a narrow panel (form.jpg). Staff groups are bordered sections with the Sign out button aligned right (staff.jpg). Nothing overlaps or clips. One card button wraps to two lines ("Book Red Wine Cellar Tour", start.jpg), which makes card buttons uneven. The confirmation panel stretches full width with much empty space on the right.
evidence.usability: Booking takes one click and one form, with the tasting details repeated above the form, an "All tastings" back link, and a "Back to all tastings" button on success. Staff reach the page via the footer link, and empty groups say "No bookings yet". Issues: Cancel deletes immediately with no confirmation or undo (Staff.tsx:85,113-125), and a fully booked tasting still offers a submittable form.
evidence.reception: Guests would find it trustworthy and on-brand, and staff get a clear, responsive list. Raw ISO dates, the lack of tasting descriptions and imagery, and instant irreversible cancellation keep it from feeling fully polished for a winery's public site.

strengths: Robust server: synchronous seat check that is proven safe under concurrent requests, and one zod schema shared by client and server with errors under the field they concern
Strong staff security: timing-safe password comparison, session regeneration, fixed lifetime, rate-limited sign-in, hardened cookies and helmet
Meaningful API and end-to-end tests covering every brief requirement, plus good accessibility (aria-describedby errors, focus management, skip link)
issues: Staff Cancel deletes a booking immediately with no confirmation or undo (Staff.tsx:85,113-125), so one misclick loses a guest's booking
Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, no release/versioning or changelog, no staff manual, and a loose Node version (engines >=22, no .nvmrc)
Polish gaps: raw ISO dates, a fully booked tasting still shows a submittable form, "Only 1 seats left" grammar (booking-schema.ts:31), and a low-contrast gold focus ring
review.verdict: This is a well-engineered, secure and well-tested booking app that meets every requirement in the brief and looks like a small winery's site. Before shipping I would add a confirmation step to Cancel, a CI pipeline and a short staff guide, and fix the minor text and date-format details.
